questions.q: In the production of home-made local soap, which two primary ingredients are chemically reacted together?
options: Vinegar and baking soda
Palm oil (or any fat) and an alkali (such as caustic soda or potash)
Lemon juice and common salt
Bleach and perfume
questions.explain: Soap making (saponification) requires the chemical reaction between a fat or oil (like palm oil) and a strong alkali (like caustic soda or local potash).

questions.q: Which of the following acidic liquids is often used as a home-made solvent for cleaning glass and removing grease?
options: Milk
Vinegar
Palm wine
Honey
questions.explain: Vinegar contains acetic acid, making it an excellent, non-toxic natural solvent for cutting through grease and cleaning surfaces like glass.

questions.q: When applying home-made polish to wooden furniture, it is recommended to use:
options: A piece of hard sandpaper
A wet and soapy sponge
A soft, clean, and dry cloth
A steel wool scouring pad
questions.explain: A soft, clean cloth (lint-free) is used to apply furniture polish to avoid scratching the wood while ensuring an even spread and shine.

questions.q: Why must excess polish be thoroughly rubbed off after applying it to furniture?
options: To allow the wood to rot properly.
Because leaving it on will make the surface sticky and attract dust.
To change the original color of the wood permanently.
So the polish can be squeezed out and reused.
questions.explain: If polish is left thickly on furniture, it creates a sticky residue that traps dust and dirt instead of keeping the surface clean and shiny.

questions.q: What is the primary difference between a deodorant and an antiperspirant?
options: Deodorants mask odor, while antiperspirants contain ingredients that block pores to reduce sweating.
Deodorants are used on the feet, while antiperspirants are only for the hair.
Deodorants cause sweating, while antiperspirants are only perfumes.
There is no difference; they are exactly the same product.
questions.explain: While deodorants target and mask body odor caused by bacteria, antiperspirants actively reduce the amount of sweat produced by blocking the sweat glands.

NNPC
NAFDAC
FRSC
questions.explain: NAFDAC (National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control) issues a unique registration number (NAFDAC Reg. No.) to certified cosmetic products to guarantee their safety and quality.

questions.q: When producing home-made body creams or pomades, heat is often required to melt the waxes and oils. Which method is safest to prevent burning the ingredients?
options: Heating them directly over an open, high flame
Using a double boiler (placing the ingredients in a bowl over boiling water)
Putting them in an open fire with dry wood
Leaving them outside in the sun for a month
questions.explain: Using a double boiler ensures gentle and even heating, preventing delicate oils and waxes from burning, catching fire, or losing their beneficial properties.

options: Kerosene
Shea butter
Wood ash
Battery acid
questions.explain: Shea butter, extracted from the nuts of the shea tree, is a natural fat rich in vitamins and is highly valued as a base ingredient for moisturizing skin creams.

questions.q: To ensure cosmetic safety, what is a 'patch test'?
options: Testing a cosmetic product by applying a small amount to a patch of skin to check for allergic reactions.
Sewing a small patch of fabric onto clothing using a cosmetic cream.
Applying a thick layer of makeup to cover an eye patch.
Submitting the product to the police for chemical testing.
questions.explain: A patch test involves applying a small amount of a cosmetic product to an inconspicuous area of skin and waiting 24-48 hours to ensure it does not cause irritation or an allergic reaction.

questions.q: Which of the following toxic ingredients should NEVER be included in cosmetics because it dangerously lightens (bleaches) the skin and causes organ damage?
options: Vitamin E
Coconut oil
Hydroquinone (in high unauthorized doses)
Aloe vera gel
questions.explain: Hydroquinone and heavy metals like mercury are dangerous skin-bleaching agents banned or heavily restricted by NAFDAC because they cause severe skin damage, cancer, and organ failure.

questions.q: Proper storage is essential for home-made cosmetics. How should a batch of home-made deodorant generally be stored to maintain its quality?
options: In an open bowl left outside in the rain
In an airtight container kept in a cool, dry place
Next to a hot cooking stove
Mixed in with dirty laundry
questions.explain: Cosmetics, especially home-made ones without strong artificial preservatives, should be stored in clean, airtight containers in a cool and dry environment to prevent melting and bacterial growth.

questions.q: A regulatory body enforces rules such as expiration dates on cosmetics. Why is it dangerous to use expired cosmetics?
options: They become illegal to touch and attract high fines.
The active ingredients break down, and harmful bacteria or mold may have grown inside them.
The packaging permanently seals shut after the date passes.
They turn into pure alcohol.
questions.explain: Expired cosmetics can undergo chemical changes making them ineffective, and the preservatives break down, allowing harmful bacteria and mold to thrive which can cause infections.

questions.q: When making pomade (hair cream) at home, after melting the petroleum jelly and wax, why must essential oils or perfumes be added only after the mixture has slightly cooled?
options: Because perfumes will freeze the mixture immediately.
Because adding them to boiling liquid will cause the volatile fragrances to evaporate and lose their scent.
Because it will change the color of the pomade to black.
Because the mixture will turn into hard soap.
questions.explain: Essential oils and perfumes are highly volatile. If added while the wax is too hot, they evaporate quickly into the air, leaving the finished pomade scentless.

questions.q: Which local substance is traditionally used as an antiperspirant or water purifier because of its natural astringent and antibacterial properties?
options: Alum (Potassium aluminum sulfate)
Red mud
Camphor balls
Granulated sugar
questions.explain: Alum is a natural mineral known for its astringent properties. It tightens skin pores to reduce sweating, kills odor-causing bacteria, and is also used to clarify murky water.

questions.q: Lemon juice is often used as a home-made cleaning agent primarily because it contains:
options: Hydrochloric acid that burns through metal.
Citric acid, which acts as a natural mild bleach and dissolves hard water stains and grease.
Heavy oils that polish wooden floors permanently.
High amounts of sugar that make surfaces sticky.
questions.explain: Lemons contain a high concentration of citric acid, giving them antibacterial properties and the ability to cut through grease, dissolve mineral stains, and act as a mild, safe bleach.
